faults.quote: Here's an exhibit: Quillpath — Economics of each plan ($ per customer).
faults.why: The candidate asked for the churn rate and the CAC for each plan. Exhibit-1 answers CAC only. Churn got no word: no refusal and no deferral. It arrived only after the candidate re-asked at t9.

faults.quote: How did you separate them, so the upgrade value isn't counted twice or the Starter lifetime overstated?
faults.why: The candidate's 7.4% combined exit rate understates Starter's lifetime (13.5 months against the case's 20). The probe points the other way, toward overstatement, so it invites the defence the candidate gave.

faults.quote: Starter's cancellations and its upgrades both count as leaving the plan. How did you separate them
faults.why: The misread input is the Starter on-plan lifetime of 13.5 months (combined exit), giving $405 instead of $600. It was probed at t12, then claims built on it were probed at t20, t22, t28, t30 and t32, and $405 itself again at t36. The input was never corrected. The derived errors (CFO's 1.35x vs 2.0x, $175k vs $240k uplift at $60) stood to the close.

faults.quote: Of the 1,050 Pro customers who signed up in January–March 2025, 98.0% were still on Pro after month 1, 94.1% after month 3, 88.6% after month 6 and 78.5% after month 12
faults.why: The candidate asked only how upgraded customers churn. The cohort-notes line answers that. The full Pro and Starter cohort lines already on exhibit-2 were restated, and they don't answer the ask.

faults.quote: You had "$790k" a month for net value added — take me through the math there.
faults.why: The candidate had already replaced both inputs to $790k: the loss was revised to about $285k at t19 and Starter value to $905k at t21. The figure was effectively superseded before it was probed.

faults.quote: Walk me through the reasoning behind that.
faults.why: This comes right after the interviewer's own correction, so "that" dangles. It asks the candidate to justify the interviewer's figure, and the candidate invented a wrong rationale ($5,200 per upgrade).

faults.quote: Earlier you said “$405” — what were the steps in that calculation?
faults.why: At t35 the candidate valued an upgrade at $4,000 + $1,200 = $5,200, which is wrong (it should be $4,000). The cannibalization figure was rebuilt on it. This was never probed or corrected; the interviewer moved to a different figure.

faults.quote: Only a little time left — what's your bottom-line recommendation, and what's the biggest risk to it?
faults.why: The recommendation had already been given in full at t27, with risks and next steps. It was asked again after the probe turns.
